newsitem.title: UK: Tabloids tell Philip to "zip lip" after gun gaffe.
newsitem.headline: Tabloids tell Philip to "zip lip" after gun gaffe.

text.p: British tabloids united on Friday to condemn Prince Philip for his gaffe on the Dunblane school massacre, saying he was a grumpy old aristocrat who should "zip his lip".

Queen Elizabeth's blunt-spoken husband sparked uproar when he compared guns to cricket bats and dismissed the clamour for new gun controls after social misfit Thomas Hamilton killed 16 children and their teacher last March in the Scottish town of Dunblane.

"You are an arrogant, over-bearing, insensitive, tactless, patronising, selfish, boorish, out-of-touch and now sickening fool," the Daily Mirror said in a "Zip up the lip" open letter to Prince Philip after a controversial radio interview.
The Sun was equally blunt in an editorial, saying: "Prince Philip is a grumpy 75-year-old aristocrat who is totally detached from reality. In future he should try to keep his stupidity a secret."
Philip expressed sympathy for the victims' relatives but said public and government reaction had not been wholly rational.

"If a cricketer, for instance, suddenly decided to go into a school and batter a lot of people to death with a cricket bat, which he could do very easily, I mean are you going to ban cricket bats?" he said in a BBC radio interview.
Philip later apologised for criticising government plans to ban most handguns in the wake of the massacre and saying shooting club members were no more dangerous than golfers.
Relatives of the dead and injured children were outraged by the interview, saying he had been crass and insensitive.
"Your apology is another insult to us all in Dunblane," said Christine McSkimming, whose granddaughter was crippled in the school massacre.

Hamilton turned his gun on himself and committed suicide, prompting one reader of the London Times to ask in its letter columns; "Perhaps the duke has not considered how Hamilton could turn a cricket bat on himself?"

The Greek-born prince has been embroiled in controversy before over his comments and former Liberal leader Sir David Steel said of the latest faux pas: "The Duke of Edinburgh's problem is that he was born with a silver foot in his mouth."
During a visit to China in 1986 he described Beijing as "ghastly" and told British students: "If you stay here much longer you'll all be slitty-eyed."
In 1995, the one-time sailor asked a Scottish driving instructor: "How do you keep the natives off the booze (drink) long enough to pass the test?"
He once said of Canada: "We don't come here for our health. We can think of other ways of enjoying ourselves."
